interest: Shows 1949 Taiwan sugar trade supplying occupied Japan and global markets amid Communist takeover of Shanghai commerce.
overview: This file (State Department decimal 894.61351) covers sugar production, trade, and related agricultural commodities in East Asia between October 1948 and November 1949, with a primary focus on occupied Japan's sugar procurement from Taiwan (Formosa) and post-war regional sugar commerce. The records comprise outgoing and incoming diplomatic telegrams exchanged between the Department of State in Washington and overseas posts in Manila, Tokyo, Shanghai, and Taipei. They document Taiwan Sugar Corporation's post-war production recovery, domestic pricing issues, and major export sales to SCAP for Japan, Great Britain, Egypt, Syria, and Southeast Asia, as well as cargo shipping to Yokohama. The file also incorporates economic intelligence on sugar stocks and commodity taxes in Communist-controlled Shanghai, beet sugar mills in Manchuria, and an apparently misfiled military cable regarding Economic Cooperation Administration (ECA) cotton financing under the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund (OJEIRF).

subfiles.about: Lovett instructs the Embassy in Manila to cable latest estimates for 1948-49 Philippine sugar production and 1949 prospective arrivals.
subfiles.summary: State asks Manila for 1948-49 and 1949 sugar production and shipment estimates for the Agriculture Department.
subfiles.title: Outgoing telegram from Lovett to Manila requesting sugar estimates

subfiles.about: SCAP Tokyo outlines banking channels and letters of credit for ECA cotton purchases under the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo relays Army financing terms for ECA cotton purchases via three US banks, with payment through SCAP's commercial account.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from Tokyo on ECA cotton purchase financing

subfiles.about: Sebald reports that the ship Hai Sui will enter Yokohama from Takao with 9,000 tons of sugar.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports a ship will unload 9,000 tons of Taiwan sugar at Yokohama in September 1949.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from Sebald (Tokyo) on sugar shipment from Takao

subfiles.about: Shanghai reports data on Shanghai sugar stocks and prices, Manchurian beet sugar mills, and Taiwan Sugar Company production and exports.
subfiles.from: Walter P. McConaughy (for Peaslee), American Consulate General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Shanghai reports Communist-controlled sugar stocks, pricing, and a new commodity tax, plus Manchurian beet-sugar output and Taiwan's 1948-49 production and exports to SCAP, Britain, Syria, and Egypt.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from McConaughy (Shanghai) on sugar supply, pricing, and Taiwan/Manchuria production

subfiles.about: MacDonald transmits a comprehensive report from Taipei on Taiwan sugar production, export contracts, crop acreage, and fertilizer distribution.
subfiles.from: Donald G. MacDonald, American Consulate, Taipei
subfiles.summary: MacDonald details Taiwan's 1948-49 sugar output and exports to many countries including Japan, forecasting a drop as farmers shift fertilizer to rice and plant lower-yield cane.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from MacDonald (Taipei) on Taiwan sugar production and export estimates
